methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional capacity-building in a non-metro region, creating potential for deep, distributed AI fluency beyond traditional tech hubs if it can develop sustainable peer learning networks.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops by a Norfolk native directly address the distribution challenge, signaling grassroots capability-building that could spread deep fluency through peer networks rather than platform dependency.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Commentary explicitly naming the urban-rural divide around data centers signals recognition that AI infrastructure concentration in NoVA may extract resources from rural areas without distributing capability or economic benefit.

signals.title: Richmond summer program helps visually impaired students explore careers in technology and cybersecurity - WTVR.com
signals.signal_reading: Specialized tech/cybersecurity program for visually impaired students shows Richmond Metro developing targeted deep capability initiatives, but its specialized nature signals concentrated rather than broadly distributed skill development.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech adding an AI minor to curriculum creates foundational educational infrastructure in the New River Valley that could seed distributed deep expertise if graduates disperse regionally rather than migrating to metro hubs.
